message.content:
Second independent check. Is this M12 code-review finding a REAL, actionable bug/issue that should be fixed before merge? Read the code yourself. Be skeptical — confirm only if you can point to the concrete problem in the diff.

Lens: a11y
File: app/(customer)/account/page.tsx (Receipts StatusBadge, lines 174-178: <StatusBadge>{p.status}</StatusBadge>)
Title: Payment status rendered as raw machine enum, unlocalized and read verbatim
Detail: The badge prints p.status directly, so the payment_status enum values "authorized" / "captured" / "refunded" / "failed" (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:634) are shown as-is and spoken verbatim by a screen reader. This is a raw token rather than human-readable copy and violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing strings via messages/en.json) — every other status in the diff (bookings, availability) goes through a localized label map. Additionally a "failed" payment renders with tone="neutral" (grey), so a failure is not visually distinguished from a normal non-captured state; meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.

content.text:
This confirms the finding completely. There is no payment status label map anywhere in the codebase — `p.status` is rendered raw in the receipts badge (line 177). Interestingly, the booking status keys (`statusConfirmed`, etc.) exist in en.json but aren't actually used in any component currently — but that doesn't change the core issue: payment status is rendered as a raw enum token, and there's a localized-label convention in the project that it bypasses.

Let me verify the second part of the claim about the `tone` logic — that a "failed" payment renders as `tone="neutral"` (grey). Looking at line 175: `tone={p.status === "captured" ? "success" : "neutral"}`. So `authorized`, `refunded`, AND `failed` all get `tone="neutral"`. This confirms a failed payment is visually indistinguishable from a normal non-captured state (e.g. authorized). The meaning rests entirely on the lowercase token text.

Let me also confirm the StatusBadge here has no icon (the badge's own doc comment says meaning should be carried by "icon + text label together"). Looking at line 174-178, the receipts StatusBadge passes no `icon` prop, unlike the booking badge which passes `icon={CalendarClock}`. So for the receipts badge, meaning rests on text alone, and that text is a raw lowercase machine token.

All claims in the finding are verified:

1. **Raw enum rendered verbatim** — Confirmed. Line 177 prints `{p.status}` directly. The `payment_status` enum values (`authorized`/`captured`/`refunded`/`failed`, per database.types.ts:634) are shown literally and would be spoken verbatim by a screen reader.

2. **Violates CLAUDE.md rule 7** (all user-facing strings via `messages/en.json`) — Confirmed. There are no payment-status label keys anywhere in en.json, and no label map exists in the codebase. The project does have a localized-status convention (the `account.statusConfirmed`/`statusCompleted`/etc. keys exist for booking statuses), so this badge is an inconsistent outlier.

3. **`failed` renders as `tone="neutral"` (grey)** — Confirmed. Line 175: `tone={p.status === "captured" ? "success" : "neutral"}` lumps `failed` with `authorized`/`refunded` as neutral grey. A failed payment is not visually distinguished, and with no icon passed, meaning rests solely on the lowercase token text — which also brushes against the "no meaning by color alone / icon+text together" principle baked into the StatusBadge component's own doc comment.

This is a real, actionable issue and it is concrete: the fix is to map each `payment_status` value to a localized label and an appropriate tone (especially distinguishing `failed`/`refunded`), matching how the rest of the app handles statuses.

content.text:
I've confirmed this is a real, actionable a11y/i18n bug. Summary:

- **File**: `/Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/app/(customer)/account/page.tsx` lines 174-178.
- **Raw enum**: line 177 renders `{p.status}` directly; the `payment_status` enum (`authorized`/`captured`/`refunded`/`failed`, defined in `database.types.ts:634`) is shown and read verbatim by screen readers.
- **Rule 7 violation**: I grepped the codebase and `messages/en.json` — no payment-status label keys or label map exist anywhere, while booking statuses do have localized keys (`account.statusConfirmed`, etc.), making this an inconsistent outlier.
- **Tone problem**: line 175 `tone={p.status === "captured" ? "success" : "neutral"}` makes `failed` indistinguishable from `authorized`/`refunded`, and the badge passes no icon, so meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.
